findings.issue: 99: a note deleted or renamed outside the app is recreated by the next autosave
findings.damage: After an agent renames or deletes a note that is open in a tab, the owner's next keystroke (or a calendar drag) writes the whole tab buffer back to the old path. A delete is undone, and after a rename the owner's new typing goes into a resurrected copy at the old path while the renamed file never gets it. The note's content ends up split across two files with the same title, wikilinks get ambiguous, and nothing in the UI says so. No bytes are destroyed, but the owner has to find and merge the two copies by hand, and a later cleanup of the 'duplicate' can delete the typing.
findings.likelihood: Occasional, and it follows directly from the owner's stated workflow. The natural trigger is asking an agent to 'rename/split/merge this note' while it is open, then typing on in that tab. An external rename of a single file reports the old path (it has a dot), so reloadExternallyChangedTabs reaches it, the read rejects, the rejection is only logged at debug level, and the tab stays bound to the dead path. A clean tab that nobody types in does no harm. The external folder-rename variant fails loudly (missing parent, a toast and a retry every 5 s), so it does not count here.
findings.evidence: src/lib/core/editor/editor.service.ts:439-442 (a rejected read logs debug and continues, the tab is kept); :194 writeTextFile(path, content) with no options (plugin-fs default create:true); :428 dirty tabs are skipped entirely; src/lib/app/lifecycle/app-lifecycle.service.ts:486-492 (the watcher batch only reloads tabs and rebuilds indexes); closeTabsForDeletedPath is called only from path-change.service.ts:159 (in-app ops); frontmatter-write.service.ts:153 uses create:false only in the closed-note branch
findings.argument: I checked the code at HEAD: no watcher path closes or orphans a tab whose file disappeared, and every tab save uses create:true. The audit left it out as 'no bytes lost, corner case', and it ignored a strong challenge to add it. The challenge's argument about colliding with 98 in writeTab no longer holds, because 98 was narrowed and leaves writeTab alone. The case still matters on its own: the owner explicitly lets agents edit the vault from outside and puts file system operations first. The fix is frontend only and S to M: create:false in writeTab, plus closing a clean tab or orphaning a dirty one on a not-found reload. It edits reloadExternallyChangedTabs, which first-wave 98 also edits, so give it 'Blocked by: 98' instead of running it in parallel.

findings.issue: 157 (from 124): an external folder move or a bulk edit of more than 10 notes leaves the indexes stale until the vault is reopened
findings.damage: After an agent moves a folder, rebuildAllIndexes returns early because the batch holds only directory paths (dot-less basenames). The Rust VaultIndex, FTS5 and semantic rows keep the notes at their old paths until the vault is reopened, so views, QueryJS, backlinks and search show ghost paths and miss the moved notes. After a scripted edit of more than 10 files in one batch, the full branch rebuilds the VaultIndex but never updates FTS5 or semantic rows, so text and semantic search show stale snippets. No content is lost.
findings.likelihood: Occasional with agents. A scripted bulk edit (sed or a refactor across many notes) or `mv` of a folder lands in one watcher batch. Agents editing files one by one over several seconds go through the incremental path, which is correct. Whether FSEvents reports the children of a renamed directory is OS behavior I did not verify; the code path that drops directory-only batches is confirmed.
findings.evidence: src/lib/app/lifecycle/watcher-handler.service.ts:36-47 (directory-only early return), :56 (incremental only up to 10 files), :71-78 (the full branch has no update_search_index_file or semantic call); src/lib/core/filesystem/fs.watcher.ts handleChangedPaths passes the raw changedPaths to notifyListeners
findings.argument: This is a real gap in reactivity for the owner's agent workflow, but it only makes data on screen stale, it heals on vault reopen, and 157 is still needs-triage with no criteria. It should be triaged next, not forced into this wave.

findings.issue: 05 part F92: right-clicking (or Ctrl+clicking) a rendered task checkbox toggles the task
findings.damage: A task flips between [ ] and [x] without being asked and is autosaved. It is visible (the context menu then reveals the raw marker) and Cmd+Z undoes it. The other parts of 05 (a language switch deletes title="...", TSV paste of tab-indented code) are also undoable.

findings.evidence: src/lib/core/markdown-editor/extensions/live-preview/widgets.ts:41-47 (the mousedown listener calls preventDefault and dispatches for every button, with no e.button or isMacContextClick check; the wikilink listener in the same file guards it)

findings.issue: 19: wikilink autocomplete inserts an image or PDF without its extension
findings.damage: Picking photo.png from the `![[` popup inserts `![[photo]]`. That becomes a note embed, which readTextFile shows as binary garbage instead of the image. The owner has to type the extension by hand. Nothing is written wrongly to other notes.
findings.likelihood: Every time an image or PDF is embedded through autocomplete. That is daily only if the owner embeds existing attachments this way; pasting an image is a separate path.
findings.evidence: src/lib/core/markdown-editor/extensions/wikilink/completion.ts:70-80 (label and insert are file.nameWithoutExt for every candidate); src/lib/app/editor-host.ts:78 (candidates include every link-target file, not only .md)
findings.argument: This is a reproducible daily-editor annoyance with an obvious workaround and no data effect. It is a good early second-wave pick, together with 10 and 18 on image display, but not critical.

findings.issue: 127: a note with an unquoted `up: [[Home]]` refuses every property, meta-bind, Cmd+D/Cmd+E and icon write
findings.damage: On such notes every meta-bind toggle, select or button, every Properties edit, favorite or organized toggle and every archive is refused with a 'nested values' toast. Nothing is lost or corrupted, but meta-bind, a daily flow, stops working on those notes.
findings.likelihood: It depends on agents or hand edits writing unquoted wikilinks in frontmatter. That is plausible for agents, though Obsidian and the app's own writers quote them.
findings.evidence: src/lib/core/frontmatter/properties.logic.ts:404-437 (detectLossyFrontmatter parses without foldUnquotedWikilinks, and a sequence ancestor gives 'nested'), :249 (the read side folds); writers refuse at frontmatter-write.service.ts:125-126 and widgets.ts:874
findings.argument: The failure is loud and loses nothing, so it is a ux issue. It is cheap (pure logic, frontend only, owner decision recorded) and worth doing early if the owner sees agent-written unquoted links in practice. It does not belong in a content-safety wave.

findings.issue: 119: a non-UTF-8 or unlisted binary file opened in the editor is written back as U+FFFD text
findings.damage: The worst damage among the left-out Issues: the original bytes of a .docx, .xlsx, .sqlite or Latin-1 .md file are replaced for good, and File History holds nothing earlier.
findings.likelihood: Rare. It needs a click on an unlisted binary in the folder lens (or a legacy-encoded note) and then a keystroke that changes the text. Nobody types into a buffer that shows binary garbage, and on macOS agents write UTF-8.
findings.evidence: src/lib/core/filesystem/fs.logic.ts:95-104 (BINARY_FILE_EXTENSIONS has no office or db formats); src/lib/core/editor/editor.service.ts:194 (writes tab.content verbatim)
findings.argument: The damage is severe but the trigger needs a deliberate edit of garbage text, so damage times likelihood stays low. Leaving it out is right. The same goes for 100, 105, 107, 109, 120 and 121: I checked their triggers, and each needs millisecond races, a full disk, dropped FSEvents, case-mismatched folders or CRLF files, none of which this owner hits in normal use.

bottom_line: Only Issue 99 from outside the first wave is critical enough to stake the plan on, and I checked it in the code at HEAD. When a note open in a tab is renamed or deleted outside the app, the tab is not closed or marked, and its save uses writeTextFile's default create:true. So the owner's next keystroke recreates the note at its old path, and after a rename their typing ends up in a ghost file that the renamed note never gets. That follows directly from the owner's stated workflow of agents editing the vault. The objection that it would collide with 98 in writeTab no longer applies, since 98 was narrowed and leaves writeTab alone. Add 99 with 'Blocked by: 98', because both rewrite reloadExternallyChangedTabs. The next tier loses no content: 157 (external folder moves and bulk edits of more than 10 notes leave the indexes stale until the vault is reopened; it still needs criteria), 05-F92 (a right-click on a task checkbox toggles it), 19 (autocomplete embeds an image as a note) and 127 (an unquoted wikilink in frontmatter blocks meta-bind writes on that note). They are cheap and good early second-wave picks, but not critical. The remaining left-out content Issues (100, 105, 107, 109, 119, 120, 121) need races, a full disk, dropped FSEvents, case-mismatched paths or unusual encodings, so leaving them out is right. Nothing was run; every verdict comes from reading the code at 4b122b303.

must_fix_before_use.issue: Issue 10 (first wave, size S): the asset-protocol scope in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:31-44 lists $HOME/kokobrain-vault/** (singular) but not $HOME/kokobrain-vaults/**. Confirmed at HEAD. Every embedded image (![[pic.png]], ![](...), Quick Capture screenshots) in a vault under ~/kokobrain-vaults shows as broken. The fix adds two glob lines and needs a rebuild. Issue 14 (canvas image nodes, no fs:allow-read-file in capabilities/default.json, also confirmed) can ship in the same build if you use image nodes, but canvas image and file nodes also need Issue 15 before they preview.
must_fix_before_use.why: This is the only item I would fix today, and it is not a content risk: the image files are intact and only their display fails. It is on the list because it fails on the first note with an image, on every image, with no message, and the fix takes minutes. You can skip it only if the vault lives under ~/Documents/kokobrain-vaults ($DOCUMENT/** already covers that path) and ~/Documents is not synced by iCloud Desktop & Documents. Otherwise moving the vault there would break your 'no sync tool' assumption. The audit says only ~/kokobrain-vaults exists on this machine, so your vault is very likely affected.

precautions.habit: Quit with Cmd+Q (or the app menu's Quit). Never use the red close button. Before logout, shutdown, restart or a macOS update, quit Kokobrain with Cmd+Q first, and do not quit from the Dock menu. If you hit the red button by mistake, press Cmd+Q and relaunch before your next capture.
precautions.why: Cmd+Q, app-menu Quit, the red button and Restart to update all run prepareForExit (exit.service.ts:15-23: save every dirty tab, ask only when a save fails, drain calendar writes, flush settings). But the red button then destroys the main window, and lib.rs:393 has no Reopen handler. The app sits with no window, and every clipboard capture or deep link is silently dropped (the dedupe anchor advances, so retrying with the same clipboard does nothing). Dock Quit, logout and shutdown skip the flush and lose up to the last 2 s of typing, or 10 s in a continuous run.

precautions.habit: Do not type in a note while an AI agent is editing that same note. Close its tab before asking an agent to edit, rename, move or delete it, or at least stop typing in it and wait about 3 s so autosave has run and the tab is clean. After an agent reorganizes files, look for old-path notes that came back.
precautions.why: reloadExternallyChangedTabs (editor.service.ts:428) skips a dirty tab, and writeTab (:194) writes with no disk check. An agent write that lands while you have unsaved typing in that note is overwritten with no copy anywhere: File History never snapshots external writes. Even after first-wave Issue 98 lands, an autosave that fires before the watcher event (about 500 ms + 300 ms) still overwrites the agent's write without a copy, because that case is the non-first-wave Issue 153. With agents in your workflow this is more likely than the audit's 'corner case' rating, which assumed no second writer. An agent rename or delete of an open note is undone by the next keystroke, because writeTextFile creates the file (99). On a clean tab the reload works, but the caret keeps its old offset (01, below).

precautions.habit: Put the vault under local git: no remote is needed, so nothing syncs. Commit often, for example an hourly launchd job running 'git add -A && git commit -q -m auto', or have agents commit before and after their edits. Add .kokobrain/kokobrain.db* to .gitignore. Never run git checkout, reset, stash or pull in the vault while Kokobrain has notes from it open.
precautions.why: Every gap in the in-app safety nets below comes back to 'only Time Machine or git can recover this': agent versions overwritten, notes with no snapshot, history hidden after a rename, a truncated write, an overwritten canvas or settings file. The watcher already ignores .git (watcher.rs:55-78), so commits cause no index churn. Operations that rewrite the working tree while tabs are open trigger Issues 99 and 100 (resurrected files, dropped-FSEvents rescans), so keep those for when the app is closed.

precautions.habit: Settings > File History: raise Retention days from 7 to something like 90 (365 at most). Select the field and type the number, then check the value it shows. Turn on Snapshot backup only if you do not use git.
precautions.why: cleanup_history runs at every vault open, and delete_old_snapshots (history_repo.rs:82-89) deletes every row older than retention + 30 days, the newest one included. At the default 7, any note not edited in the app for 37 days has no history at all. Every autosave stores a full copy for the retention period, so a long retention makes kokobrain.db grow. The input clamps on every keystroke (Issue 82), so clearing the field first gives 1. Snapshot backup writes .md copies that survive retention and renames, but nothing cleans them up.

precautions.habit: After Cmd+D (favorite) or Cmd+E (organized), and after a clean open note was reloaded because an agent or a rename changed it, click where you want to type before typing. If typed text lands in the wrong place, press Cmd+Z.
precautions.why: Confirmed at HEAD: the content-sync effect reads the old caret offset (MarkdownEditor.svelte:627), and replaceDoc passes it as an explicit unmapped selection (:184). After a frontmatter write above the caret, the next keystrokes land about 16 characters off, and autosave writes them. The typing is normal history, so Cmd+Z undoes it.

precautions.habit: In a note with properties, do not use Cmd+Up (document start) and then type, press Enter or press Delete. Do not press or hold Backspace at the very start of the first body line. If raw YAML or a stray --- line suddenly shows at the top, press Cmd+Z at once. To remove the risk completely, turn off the 'Properties block' decorator in Settings > Troubleshooting: the frontmatter then shows as plain text you can see while editing.
precautions.why: Confirmed at HEAD: rg finds no atomicRanges, transactionFilter or changeFilter under src/lib, and only mouse clicks are kept out of the hidden fence. Keyboard edits break the --- fences, the block then reads as body text, and autosave writes it. The break shows on screen and Cmd+Z undoes it; File History also holds the version from before the break.

precautions.habit: Kanban: always press Enter (or click elsewhere) to commit a card or lane-title edit before you switch tabs, press Cmd+W or quit. Canvas: after typing in a card, click the background or wait a second before Cmd+W or Cmd+Q.
precautions.why: KanbanView is still unkeyed and writes through onContentChange into tabs[activeIndex] (EditorView.svelte:80, confirmed). An open card edit lives only in the textarea, so a keyboard tab switch or a close either drops it or writes the board's markdown into the note now in front. A canvas edit sits in a 300 ms debounce, and the tab is not dirty yet, so closeTab neither prompts nor saves, and the edit is dropped.

precautions.habit: If 'This file has unsaved changes. Discard changes?' appears when you close a tab, click Cancel, wait 2 s and close again (or press Cmd+S before Cmd+W). Never click Discard Changes to dismiss it.
precautions.why: closeTab (editor.service.ts:311-320) prompts for any dirty tab and does not save first. If you click Discard before the 2 s autosave fires, the last typing is gone. For the same reason, press Cmd+S before Duplicate, so the copy is not missing the last typing (112).

precautions.habit: In live preview, right-click the task text, never the checkbox. Change the language of a code block that has attributes (```python title="x") by editing the fence text, not with the dropdown. Paste tab-indented code or web content with links in source mode (Cmd+\, paste, Cmd+\).
precautions.why: Confirmed at HEAD: the checkbox mousedown (widgets.ts:41-47) toggles and saves on any mouse button. The dropdown replaces the whole info string, so title="..." is lost. The TSV and HTML paste handlers live in the live-preview extension, which source mode removes, so a paste there arrives verbatim. Type values into meta-bind number and date inputs instead of pasting them (40), because the paste lands in the note text. Each of these shows on screen and Cmd+Z undoes it.

precautions.habit: Edit your Quick Capture template: drop 'title: <% title %>' (link captures inject a correctly written title themselves), and move source_title to the body below the closing --- or wrap it in double quotes. Leave the URL and app-id fields as they are.
precautions.why: Values go into the frontmatter raw (deep-link-actions.ts:176-188; the shipped help/examples/templates/Quick Note.md has them unquoted). A page title with ': ' or ' #' writes broken or truncated YAML, and from then on the Properties panel, meta-bind and Cmd+D refuse that note. Double quotes still break on a title that contains " or \, so the body is the safer place.

precautions.habit: If a .canvas opens empty when it should not be, do not click Add card or edit it. Switch to its source mode (top-right button) and fix or restore the JSON. When a note does not render or typing does not mark its tab dirty, switch tabs and come back, or use Cmd+\, and stop typing in it.
precautions.why: An unparseable canvas, from an agent, a hand edit or a source-mode typo, loads as an empty canvas, and the first edit overwrites the file (canvas.logic.ts:36-49). A widget that throws on every render leaves the view out of sync with its tab, and typing is silently not stored. That second case has no known daily trigger.

precautions.habit: While the File History dialog is open, do not press Cmd+W or switch tabs, and check which note the dialog shows before you click Restore. To restore a .kanban or .canvas, switch it to source mode first.
precautions.why: restoreSnapshot dispatches into the shared editor view and saves the active tab. After a tab change it overwrites a different note. On a board view there is no editor view, so the restore closes the dialog having written nothing.

precautions.habit: Tell agents, and remember yourself: quote wikilinks in YAML (up: "[[Home]]") and never write an empty '---' '---' block. Do not open .docx, .xlsx, .epub, .sqlite or .db files from the file tree. For daily-note and deep-link writes, use append, not prepend, and do not use overwrite=true in Shortcuts.
precautions.why: Unquoted wikilinks make every frontmatter writer refuse the note, with a toast. An empty block makes later writers stack a second block. Unknown binary extensions open as text, and one keystroke autosaves U+FFFD over the file. Prepend puts the text above the frontmatter, so the note loses its properties. overwrite=true replaces a note with no snapshot of the old text.

precautions.habit: In meta-bind buttons, put updateMetadata before any open or createNote action.
precautions.why: After an open or createNote action, the shared view holds the other note, so updateMetadata writes your status into that note's frontmatter. A failed open also does not stop the remaining actions.

precautions.habit: Keep Auto Move off (the default) until Issue 36 lands. If you turn it on, keep the rules narrow, and wait about 1 s after editing a rule before you close Settings.
precautions.why: Auto Move evaluates .kanban and .canvas saves too, and moves boards and canvases that match a folder, name or tag rule. An edit to a rule made within 500 ms of closing Settings is lost at the next restart.

precautions.habit: If a toast says settings.json or the auto-move rules could not be read, quit with Cmd+Q before you change any setting, then fix or restore the file (from git).
precautions.why: After a read failure the session runs on defaults, and the first settings change, or the launch-time update check, writes those defaults over the unread file. It can also run history cleanup at the default retention. It needs a read failure, which is rare.

precautions.habit: Keep free disk space comfortable. If 'Failed to save file.' toasts appear, do not quit or discard: free space first and let the 5 s retry save. Keep the vault on the internal SSD.
precautions.why: Note writes go through plugin-fs writeTextFile, which truncates the file and then writes it. A write that fails partway (ENOSPC, or EIO on an external or network drive) leaves the note empty or truncated. Open tabs keep their text and retry; closed-note frontmatter writes do not.

precautions.habit: Treat these views as possibly wrong until their Issues land: Backlinks and Outgoing links after going back to a note (12); dashboards sorted by an optional field (17; use p.field ?? 0); numeric view filters on a property some notes lack (27); kb.pages('"Folder"') when another folder shares the name (33); search with tag: or path: (25); kanban drag inside a lane or lane drag (16; check where the card landed); tags that start with a digit or emoji (142; start tags with a letter). Also set Settings > QueryJS auto-run to manual, the in-app to-do from Issue 133.
precautions.why: None of these touches the files on disk, but each shows wrong data in a daily view. Knowing about them in advance keeps a wrong display from looking like lost notes.

safety_nets:
Checked at HEAD 4b122b303. src/ has not changed since the audit commit 5f8003d67, except TasksView and version bumps.
- Autosave (editor.service.ts:227-230): body edits save 2 s after the last keystroke, with a 10 s max wait during continuous typing; frontmatter edits save after 500 ms. saveDirtyTabs saves every dirty tab, whether active or not. A failed save shows the toast 'Failed to save file.' and retries every 5 s (:217-219), and the tab keeps its text. Cmd+S saves at once (global-keybindings.ts:76-78). Limits: no save on tab switch; canvas edits wait in a 300 ms debounce, and kanban card or lane-title edits wait in their inputs, before either reaches the tab (06, 09).
- Exit flush (exit.service.ts:15-23): Cmd+Q, app-menu Quit, the red button and Restart to update save every dirty tab, ask only when a save fails, drain calendar writes and flush settings. Limits: Dock Quit, logout, shutdown and a crash bypass it (lib.rs:393 handles only ExitRequested; Issue 106), losing at most 2 to 10 s of typing. The red button flushes but then leaves the app with no window, dropping captures (04).
- File History (on by default; .kokobrain/kokobrain.db): a snapshot of the content just written, after every successful in-app editor save, deduped by SHA-256 against the newest row. Limits: there is never a snapshot of the bytes being replaced, so a note that was never saved in the app has no history (08). External and agent writes, link rewrites and type renames are never snapshotted. Retention (7 days by default, then one per day until day 37) deletes everything older, the newest row included (history_repo.rs:82-89). Snapshots are keyed by path, so they disappear from view after a rename or move (23). Restore can write into the wrong tab, and does nothing on a board view (102, 160). The .md snapshot backup is off by default.
- Trash: in-app deletes save dirty tabs under the path first (path-change.service.ts:60) and move the item to .kokobrain/trash with a manifest. Limits: external and agent deletes bypass it, and a corrupt manifest after a crash can orphan items (114, rare).
- Undo: each tab keeps its own CodeMirror state across tab switches. External replaces (watcher reload, Cmd+D/E, link rewrite) are dispatched with addToHistory(false), so they cannot be undone, and the caret is not mapped through them (01).
- Watcher reload: an open clean tab reloads when its file changes on disk. A dirty tab is skipped ('editor always wins'), and its next save overwrites the external change with no copy (98, 153).
Nothing in the app keeps a version made outside the app. Only git or Time Machine do.
reasoning:
Short answer: you can start daily use today. No open Issue needs a code fix before use to keep your writing safe. One fix is worth doing today anyway: Issue 10, which takes two config lines and a rebuild. Without it every embedded image in a vault under ~/kokobrain-vaults is broken. That is a display failure, not data loss, but it shows on the first image you embed.

I read the PRD, the ledger and in full the Issues that can touch written content: 01-10, 13, 14, 98-102, 105-107, 115, 129, 131 and 153. I scanned the triggers and priorities of the rest. I checked these claims against the code at HEAD:
- KanbanView is still unkeyed and writes into the active tab.
- replaceDoc passes an unmapped caret position.
- No keyboard guard protects the hidden frontmatter.
- The task checkbox toggles on any mouse button.
- closeTab prompts without saving first.
- A dirty tab skips the watcher reload, and writeTab writes with no disk check.
- The run loop handles only ExitRequested, so there is no Reopen.
- The asset scope lacks $HOME/kokobrain-vaults/**, and no capability grants fs:allow-read-file.
- Retention deletes the newest snapshot.
- The watcher ignores .git.
- 'Properties block' can be turned off in Settings > Troubleshooting.

Why habits are enough: every serious content risk at HEAD needs a specific action you can avoid.
- Red button, Dock Quit or logout: 04, 106.
- Typing in a note an agent is editing: 98, 153, 105.
- Leaving a kanban card edit open while switching tabs, or Cmd+W within 300 ms of a canvas edit: 09, 06.
- Cmd+Up then Enter, or Backspace at the first body line: 02.
- Right-clicking a checkbox: 05.
- Clicking Discard Changes: 13.
- Unquoted capture titles: 03.
- Broken canvas JSON: 101.
- A tab change while File History is open: 102.
Most of these show on screen and Cmd+Z undoes them. The worst ones:
- 09 can write board markdown into another note.
- 98 silently overwrites an agent's edit.
- 107 can truncate a note when the disk is full.
None of these happens in normal use if you follow the habits.

The audit underrates one cluster for your setup: agents editing the vault. Issues 98, 153, 99 and 105 are filed as corner cases because the audit assumed no other writer, but agents are that writer. Even after first-wave Issue 98 lands, an autosave that fires before the watcher event still overwrites an agent's write with no copy, because that part is Issue 153, which is not in the first wave. Consider moving 153 up right after 98.

The single best safety net is a local git repo for the vault with frequent commits. File History cannot recover any of these:
- versions written outside the app;
- notes older than 37 days at the default retention;
- history after a rename;
- truncated writes;
- overwritten canvases or settings.

What I did not do: run the app, build anything or run any test. Two points come from the audit and were not checked in the running app: whether WebKit fires blur on removal (09), and the actual disk-full behavior (107). I could not check your vault's location or your iCloud Desktop & Documents setting.
